findings.location: What it checks, items 3–8; What it writes
findings.problem: The spec does not require validating that manifest entries are permitted by the approved module declarations and repository-boundary rules. A malformed or hostile manifest could classify arbitrary paths (including living files or `.workbench/local/` content) as module-owned, causing enrollment to baseline them and establish them as trusted ownership.
findings.suggestion: Require the existing strict manifest and declaration/write-set validation, including path boundaries, owner class, module namespace, and slot declarations; refuse the enrollment before any store write when an entry is outside the approved declarations or otherwise conflicts with repository-boundary rules.

summary: One major trust-boundary gap remains: enrollment accepts manifest ownership claims without explicitly validating them against approved declarations and path rules.
